private_note: I can't put any odds on which group I'm in, and whatever we pick lasts a generation, so I'm judging each plan by its worst case. Hazel's worst is 41, Birch 36, Alder 32, Today 22, Cedar 15. Above the bottom, Hazel's losses are moderate and its floor is a real gain. Cedar's floor is below today's. If Hazel stalls, I'd move to Alder or Birch before letting the convention fail and leave us with today's 22.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will wake up in, and none of us can even guess the odds. The choice is permanent. So I ask one question of each plan: if I turn out to be at the bottom, how badly off am I? Hazel guarantees the highest floor that can be sustained, 41 thousand, nearly double today's. Birch comes next at 36, then Alder at 32. Cedar drops the bottom to 15, with no health coverage it can count on. I won't gamble my household on that, however good the top looks. Hazel costs the upper groups something, but every group under Hazel still lives decently. Nobody under it is left in real hardship. I rank Hazel first, then Birch, then Alder. I'd rather we fail than adopt Cedar. I'm open to hearing why another plan's floor is safer, but I want a floor we can all live on.
